response.sql:
WITH race_totals AS (
  SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) as total_points
  FROM races r
  JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
avg_total AS (
  SELECT AVG(total_points) as avg_total_points
  FROM race_totals
),
above_avg_races AS (
  SELECT rt.name, rt.total_points, at.avg_total_points
  FROM race_totals rt
  CROSS JOIN avg_total at
  WHERE rt.total_points > at.avg_total_points
)
SELECT
  (SELECT SUM(total_points) FROM above_avg_races) as combined_total_points,
  (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS NUMERIC))
   FROM above_avg_races aar
   JOIN races r ON r.name = aar.name
   JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId) as average_laps_completed,
  (SELECT AVG(total_points - avg_total_points) FROM above_avg_races) as average_excess

assumptions.assumption: results.laps contains numeric or NULL values that can be safely cast to NUMERIC (documentation states it is lap number, though stored as TEXT)
"average laps completed" means the average of all laps across individual results within the filtered races, not an average of per-race averages

alternatives.interpretation: "average laps completed" could mean the average of each filtered race's average laps (i.e., compute average laps per race name, then average those per-race values)
